+
+/**
+ * Commits the change `write` makes to the published work tree `workTree` on
+ * the branch `branch`, started from the commit of `main`, pushes that branch
+ * alone, and returns the work tree to `main`. The push is a fast-forward, so it
+ * fails when `branch` holds a commit that `main` lacks. Every git runs with the
+ * HOME `home`.
+ */
+export async function pushGitBranch(
+  workTree: string,
+  home: string,
+  branch: string,
+  write: () => Promise<void>,
+): Promise<void> {
+  await runGit(workTree, home, "checkout", "-q", "-B", branch, "main");
+  await write();
+  await runGit(workTree, home, "add", "-A");
+  await runGit(workTree, home, "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "publish");
+  await runGit(workTree, home, "push", "-q", "origin", branch);
+  await runGit(workTree, home, "checkout", "-q", "main");
+}

+ * Sets the description of the manifest on the branch `branch` of the git
+ * marketplace `published` records, leaving `main` as it is (D-02). A local
+ * publication has no branch.
+ */
+export async function describeMarketplaceBranch(
+  published: PublishedMarketplace,
+  branch: string,
+  description: string,
+): Promise<void> {
+  switch (published.kind) {
+    case "dir":
+    case "file":
+      throw new Error(`a ${published.kind} publication has no branch`);
+    case "url":
+    case "github":
+      await pushGitBranch(published.root, published.gitHome, branch, () =>
+        writeMarketplaceDescription(published.manifestPath, description),
+      );
+      return;
+  }
+}
